stories.headline: Anthropic Agrees Terms of $30B Round at $900B Valuation; Sequoia, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Altimeter Co-Lead

key_facts.fact: Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia Capital and Altimeter Capital have agreed to co-lead a $30 billion round into Anthropic at a $900 billion pre-money valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia Capital and Altimeter Capital have agreed to co-lead a $30 billion round of funding into Anthropic at a $900 billion valuation before the money, according to a person with knowledge of the discussions.

key_facts.fact: The new valuation nearly triples Anthropic's last valuation of $350-380 billion fetched in a fundraising in early February.
key_facts.excerpt: The investment nearly triples its last valuation of $350 billion fetched in a fundraising in early February.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic reached $30 billion in annualized revenue earlier this month, up from roughly $10 billion in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said earlier this month that it has reached $30 billion in annualized revenue. It generated roughly $10 billion in revenue last year.

key_facts.fact: A round at this valuation would push Anthropic past OpenAI, last valued at just over $850 billion in late March.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI was valued at $852 billion in late March after closing a record-breaking $122 billion funding round.

stories.headline: xAI Launches Grok Build, an Agentic Coding CLI, in Beta for SuperGrok Heavy Subscribers

key_facts.fact: xAI launched on May 14 an early beta of Grok Build, a coding agent and CLI for professional software engineering, available first to SuperGrok Heavy subscribers.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're launching an early beta of Grok Build, a powerful new coding agent and CLI for professional software engineering and complex coding work. Available first for SuperGrok Heavy subscribers.

key_facts.fact: Grok Build supports a 'plan, review, approve' flow, MCP servers, AGENTS.md and parallel subagents that can run in their own git worktrees.
key_facts.excerpt: For complex tasks, start Grok Build in plan mode... Your AGENTS.md, plugins, hooks, skills, and MCP servers all work out of the box... For larger tasks, Grok Build delegates work to specialized subagents that run in parallel.

key_facts.fact: SuperGrok Heavy is xAI's top consumer subscription, priced at roughly $300 per month and aimed at professional developers and researchers.
key_facts.excerpt: SuperGrok Heavy was introduced alongside Grok 4 in July 2025 and is priced at roughly $300 per month, positioning it as a tier aimed at professional users, researchers, and developers.

key_facts.fact: The release positions xAI to rival Anthropic's Claude Code in agentic terminal coding tools.
key_facts.excerpt: On May 14, 2026, xAI quietly slipped a new tool into the hands of its most expensive customers... the terminal-native answer to a question the whole industry has been wrestling with: what does it actually look like when an AI stops suggesting code and starts shipping it?

sources.title: xAI Drops Grok Build: An Agentic CLI That Wants to Live in Your Terminal

stories.headline: OpenAI Brings Codex to ChatGPT Mobile App in Preview, Adds Remote SSH for Cloud Dev Environments

key_facts.fact: OpenAI rolled out a preview of Codex inside the ChatGPT mobile app on iOS and Android across all plans (including Free and Go) in supported regions on May 14.
key_facts.excerpt: Codex in the ChatGPT mobile app is rolling out in preview on iOS and Android across all plans, including Free and Go, in all supported regions.

key_facts.fact: From the phone, users can review outputs, approve commands, switch models or start new work, while files, credentials and project context stay on the connected machine where Codex runs.
key_facts.excerpt: From your phone, you can work across all of your threads, review outputs, approve commands, change models, or start something new. Your files, credentials, permissions, and local setup stay on the machine where Codex is operating.

key_facts.fact: Mobile support currently connects to the Codex app on macOS; Windows support is coming soon.
key_facts.excerpt: The feature is currently rolling out in preview across all plans, including Free and Go, in all supported regions. For now, mobile support works with the macOS Codex app. Windows support is coming soon.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the mobile rollout, Remote SSH became generally available, letting Codex connect directly into managed remote dev environments via the desktop app's SSH config.
key_facts.excerpt: Alongside the mobile rollout, Remote SSH is now generally available. It allows Codex to connect directly to managed remote environments used by development teams.

stories.headline: Calif and Anthropic's Mythos Build First Public macOS Kernel Exploit on M5 Silicon, Bypassing MIE

key_facts.fact: Calif researchers, working with Anthropic's Mythos Preview, built a working macOS kernel memory corruption exploit that bypasses Apple's Memory Integrity Enforcement (MIE) on M5 silicon — described as the first public exploit of its kind.
key_facts.excerpt: the first public macOS kernel memory corruption exploit on M5 silicon, surviving MIE... To the best of our knowledge, this is the first public macOS kernel exploit on MIE hardware.

key_facts.fact: The chain is a data-only local privilege escalation against macOS 26.4.1 that starts as an unprivileged user using only normal system calls and ends with a root shell.
key_facts.excerpt: The exploit is a data-only kernel local privilege escalation chain targeting macOS 26.4.1 (25E253). It starts from an unprivileged local user, uses only normal system calls, and ends with a root shell.

key_facts.fact: Calif says Apple spent roughly five years building MIE; its team built the exploit in five days, with bugs found on April 25 and a working exploit completed by May 1.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple spent five years building hardware and software to make memory corruption exploits dramatically harder. Our engineers, working together with Mythos Preview, built a working exploit in five days... Bruce Dang found the bugs on April 25th... by May 1st we had a working exploit.

key_facts.fact: Apple confirmed it is reviewing the 55-page report Calif delivered in person at Apple Park; CEO Thai Duong said the attack 'couldn't have been pulled off by Mythos alone'.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple is currently reviewing the report from Calif to validate its findings... Calif's chief executive, Thai Dong, said that the attack 'couldn't have been pulled off by Mythos alone and leveraged the very human cybersecurity expertise of some of Calif's hackers.'

stories.headline: Anthropic Publishes 2028 Policy Paper Urging US to Tighten Chip Controls and Curb Distillation to Hold AI Lead

key_facts.fact: In a new paper released May 14, Anthropic argues democracies can secure a commanding AI lead by 2028 if the US tightens controls on advanced compute to PRC labs, disrupts distillation of US models, and accelerates AI adoption among allies.
key_facts.excerpt: This scenario can be achieved if policymakers act now to tighten controls on advanced compute to PRC labs, disrupt their efforts to distill America's best AI models, and accelerate democracies' adoption of AI.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic warns that without action the US faces a 'destabilizing neck-and-neck race with the CCP two years from now'.
key_facts.excerpt: In advancing these policies, we are hopeful that democracies can secure a commanding lead by 2028, and avoid a destabilizing neck-and-neck race with the CCP two years from now.

key_facts.fact: The paper says PRC labs benefit from access to export-controlled US chips via smuggling and foreign data centers, and that closing those loopholes would lower China's compute ceiling and impair distillation attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: PRC labs benefit from access to export-controlled American chips via smuggling and foreign data centers, and gaps in SME controls accelerate their self-sufficiency efforts. Tightening controls and ramping up enforcement budgets can help close these loopholes... a lower compute ceiling could also materially impair distillation attacks.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also calls on the Trump administration to 'champion the export of American AI', promoting global adoption of US-developed hardware and models to deny China footholds.
key_facts.excerpt: Champion the export of American AI. As public and commercial sectors around the world increasingly adopt AI, the Trump administration should continue its efforts to promote the global adoption of trusted AI hardware and models developed and shaped by democratic principles.

sources.title: 2028: Two scenarios for global AI leadership

stories.headline: Microsoft Cancels Claude Code Licenses for Internal Devs, Mandates Shift to GitHub Copilot CLI by June 30

key_facts.fact: Microsoft is canceling thousands of internal Claude Code licenses by June 30, 2026, requiring its Experiences + Devices team to transition to GitHub Copilot CLI as the primary agentic command-line tool.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft announced plans on May 14, 2026, to discontinue internal usage of Anthropic's Claude Code tool for thousands of its developers by the end of June. The company is directing its Experiences + Devices team to transition to GitHub Copilot CLI.

key_facts.fact: The move affects engineers working on Windows, Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams and Surface; the June 30 deadline aligns with the end of Microsoft's fiscal year, suggesting cost-cutting motivation.
key_facts.excerpt: The move affects engineers working on Windows, Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, and Surface products. According to sources cited by The Verge, the June 30 deadline aligns with the final day of Microsoft's current financial year, suggesting the cancellation is partly intended to reduce operating expenses.

key_facts.fact: Rajesh Jha, EVP of Microsoft's Experiences and Devices group, said in an internal memo that 'Copilot CLI has given us something especially important: a product we can help shape directly with GitHub for Microsoft's repos, workflows, security expectations, and engineering needs'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Claude Code was an important part of that learning… at the same time, Copilot CLI has given us something especially important: a product we can help shape directly with GitHub for Microsoft's repos, workflows, security expectations, and engineering needs." Jha stated.

key_facts.fact: Internal developers reportedly favored Claude Code over GitHub Copilot CLI since Microsoft opened access in December 2025; Anthropic models remain accessible to Microsoft engineers via Copilot CLI.
key_facts.excerpt: Internal developers reportedly favored Claude Code over GitHub Copilot CLI since the company opened access in December... Despite the cancellation of Claude Code licenses, Anthropic models will remain accessible to Microsoft engineers through Copilot CLI.

stories.headline: Anthropic and Gates Foundation Pledge $200M Over Four Years to Deploy Claude in Global Health and Education

key_facts.fact: Anthropic and the Gates Foundation announced a $200 million, four-year partnership on May 14 covering global health, life sciences, education and economic mobility.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has partnered with the Gates Foundation to commit $200 million in grant funding, Claude usage credits, and technical support for programs in global health, life sciences, education, and economic mobility over the next four years.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's half is technical staff support and Claude usage credits; the Gates Foundation provides grant funding, program design and expertise.
key_facts.excerpt: Support from Anthropic's technical staff and usage credits for its Claude AI will account for its half of the financial commitment, while the Bill Gates co-founded Gates Foundation will provide grant funding, program design and expertise.

key_facts.fact: The partnership will work with the Institute for Disease Modeling on forecasting malaria and tuberculosis, and with research centers using Claude to predict drug candidates for HPV and preeclampsia.
key_facts.excerpt: They are partnering with the Institute for Disease Modeling (IDM) to improve forecasts for diseases like malaria and tuberculosis... One initiative will equip research centers to use Claude to predict drug candidates for treating HPV and preeclampsia.

key_facts.fact: The deal is roughly four times the $50 million pact the Gates Foundation announced with OpenAI in January to support 1,000 African clinics by 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: The news follows a $50 million pact that the Gates Foundation and OpenAI announced in January to support 1,000 African clinics and communities with AI by 2028.
